context: ride-safety-commissioning-led · phased delivery across an extensive, master-planned site

brief.intro: New to this project type? A theme park or entertainment complex is less a single building and more a small city: extensive site-wide infrastructure — roads, drainage, utilities, water features — threading between dozens of individually procured rides, themed structures, and food & beverage or retail buildings, usually delivered in phases so parts of the park can open while others are still under construction. Each ride is really its own specialist project: supplied, and often installed and commissioned, by its own manufacturer under structural and electrical/control interfaces the main contractor has to provide at exactly the right time. The programme's real discipline is phased-zone delivery and ride-by-ride interface management, not one continuous build. And the finish line for every ride is not construction completion but a formal ride-safety commissioning and independent inspection-authority certification — that regulatory gate, not the last coat of paint, decides when a zone can actually open to the public.

scope.name: Enabling & site-wide infrastructure
scope.desc: Earthworks, roads, drainage, utilities and water features threading across the whole site.

scope.name: Ride foundations & structural interfaces
scope.desc: Foundations and structural tie-ins for each ride package, sized and positioned to the manufacturer's specification.

scope.name: Themed structures & show sets
scope.desc: The decorative architecture and scenery built around each ride or attraction to create its theme.

scope.name: F&B / retail buildings
scope.desc: Restaurants, kiosks and shops distributed through the park.

scope.name: Back-of-house support buildings
scope.desc: Maintenance, storage and staff facilities, usually built early to support later ride installation.

scope.name: Electrical power distribution
scope.desc: Site-wide substations and MV/LV distribution, plus each ride's dedicated power and control interface.

scope.name: Mechanical — water features & utilities
scope.desc: Pumping, filtration and treatment plant serving water rides, fountains and other water features.

scope.name: Fire & life safety across the site
scope.desc: Site-wide fire-water network, alarm and suppression across themed structures and back-of-house buildings.

scope.name: Ride installation & OEM commissioning
scope.desc: Manufacturer-led delivery, installation and functional testing of each ride package.

scope.name: Testing, ride-safety certification & phased handover
scope.desc: Independent safety-authority inspection and a zone-by-zone public-opening readiness process.

must_get_right: Each ride is effectively its own sub-project supplied and commissioned by a specialist OEM — build their delivery/installation/commissioning windows into the master schedule as named interfaces, not generic activities.
Ride-safety certification by an independent inspection authority, not construction completion, is the real gate to opening — protect real time for it and for re-inspections.

Site-wide infrastructure (roads, utilities, drainage) must be substantially complete ahead of each phase/zone, because later zones depend on it — sequence phases around infrastructure readiness, not the reverse.
Themed structures and show sets are often on the critical path to a ride's opening just as much as the ride itself — coordinate their finishing with ride installation, not after it.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Each ride package and each phased opening zone is modelled as its own sub-network so ride-by-ride and zone-by-zone progress can be reported independently of the site-wide programme.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Site-wide civil and infrastructure works run a 6-day week; ride installation follows each OEM's own crew calendar, often overlapping and competing for crane/access windows; commissioning and certification run against the availability of the independent ride-safety inspection authority rather than a fixed calendar.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs site-wide infrastructure & ride foundations → themed structures/F&B shells in parallel → MEP rough-in & water features → ride OEM installation → fire/life-safety & show-control integration → OEM ride commissioning → independent ride-safety certification → phased zone handover. A slipping ride delivery cascades directly into its zone's opening date.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Ride manufacturer contracts are awarded early enough to meet each OEM's installation window; phased zone boundaries are agreed and site logistics support live construction adjacent to already-open zones; themed-structure design is frozen ahead of ride interface finalisation; mobilisation is phased to match zone sequencing.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Construction proceeds in phases adjacent to live, publicly-open park zones, requiring public-safety segregation hoarding and restricted delivery routes. Multiple ride-manufacturer OEM installation teams compete for the same crane and access windows, and specialist show-control and ride-safety commissioning engineers are shared and scarce late in each phase.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: ride-manufacturer delivery slippage cascading into a whole zone's opening date, ride-safety authority inspection scheduling outside the contractor's control, and interface changes between ride-OEM design and structural/electrical provisions. Schedule contingency is held before OEM commissioning and before ride-safety certification for each zone, rather than spread across trades.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones per phase/zone opening date) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead per ride package and per building — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
